structured.response_summary: For stronger oversight, a nonprofit board should generally establish: (1) a Governance/Nominating Committee for board composition, bylaws, policies, evaluations, succession, and conflicts of interest; (2) a Finance Committee for budgets, financial performance, reserves, investments, and long-term sustainability; (3) an independent Audit/Risk Committee for external audits, internal controls, whistleblower matters, compliance, cybersecurity, insurance, and enterprise risk; and (4) an Executive Compensation/People Committee for executive performance, compensation, succession, and workforce oversight. Depending on size and mission, it may also add Program/Impact, Development/Fundraising, Ethics/Compliance, and Investment committees. Keep committees few, chartered, appropriately independent, and subject to full-board accountability; avoid an Executive Committee unless genuinely necessary because it can concentrate authority.
